name: GitHub
description: Repos, issues and pull requests, with gh, git and the API.

signin.label: Sign in with GitHub
signin.note: Covers every repo and organization your account can reach. Uses the GitHub CLI's sign-in: you approve a code on github.com; nothing to create or paste.
signin.install: sudo apt-get install -y -qq gh || sudo dnf install -y -q gh || sudo pacman -S --noconfirm --needed github-cli
signin.command: gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --insecure-storage --scopes read:org,workflow

help: A token instead of signing in: fine-grained ones (https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens) each cover one account or organization; classic ones (https://github.com/settings/tokens) cover everything you can reach. `gh` and `git` over HTTPS both use it.
test: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user | jq -r '"Signed in as " + .login'
after: command -v gh >/dev/null && gh auth setup-git >/dev/null 2>&1; true

mcp.note: GitHub's MCP server: richer tools for issues, PRs and code search. Needs the token.

name: Fly Sprites
description: Cloud computers for heavy work: a Linux machine per project that sleeps when idle and wakes in a second.
help: Sign up at https://sprites.dev, then create a token at https://sprites.dev/account. Each Sprite has 8 vCPUs, memory that grows with the work, and 100 GB of disk; you pay for compute only while it's active. Agents use the `sprite` CLI and `sprite-job` (see skills/sprites).
test: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SPRITES_TOKEN" https://api.sprites.dev/v1/sprites | jq -r '"Connected · " + ((.sprites | length) | tostring) + " sprites" + (if .has_more then "+" else "" end)'
after: export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH; command -v sprite >/dev/null || curl -fsSL https://sprites.dev/install.sh | sh >/dev/null 2>&1; sprite auth setup --token "$SPRITES_TOKEN" >/dev/null 2>&1; true

name: Gmail
description: Your Gmail accounts, as many as you like, for Mail and agents (IMAP).
help: Each account signs in with an app password (myaccount.google.com/apppasswords; needs 2-Step Verification). If an account can't make one (some work accounts), use Sign in with Google instead.

name: Google Calendar
description: Read your calendar from its private iCal address.
help: In Google Calendar: Settings → your calendar → Integrate calendar → Secret address in iCal format. Read-only; anyone with the link can read it, so it's stored as a secret.
test: curl -fsSL "$CALENDAR_ICS_URL" | grep -c BEGIN:VEVENT | sed 's/$/ events found/'

name: Slack
description: Read channels and post as a bot you create.
help: Create an app at https://api.slack.com/apps, add bot scopes (e.g. channels:history, channels:read, chat:write), install it to your workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
test: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/auth.test | jq -r 'if .ok then "Connected to " + .team + " as " + .user else error(.error) end'

name: Telegram
description: A bot that can message you, or that you can talk to.
help: Message @BotFather on Telegram, send /newbot, and copy the token it gives you.

name: Notion
description: Read and write pages and databases you share with it.
help: Create an internal integration at https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations, copy its secret, then share the pages you want with it (… → Connections).

name: Linear
help: Linear → Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys.
test: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: $LINEAR_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"{ viewer { name } }"}' https://api.linear.app/graphql | jq -r '"Connected as " + .data.viewer.name'

name: Todoist
help: Todoist → Settings → Integrations → Developer → API token.
test: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TODOIST_API_TOKEN" https://api.todoist.com/rest/v2/projects | jq -r 'length | tostring + " projects"'

name: Home Assistant
description: Lights, sensors and automations in your home.
help: In Home Assistant: your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. The URL must be reachable from this machine (Tailscale works).

name: OpenAI API
description: For Views and scripts that call OpenAI models (images, speech, embeddings).
help: Create a key at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys. Usage is billed to that account. (Codex keeps using its own sign-in.)
test: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" https://api.openai.com/v1/models | jq -r '.data | length | tostring + " models available"'

name: Brave Search
description: Web search for agents and Views.
help: Get a key at https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com (there's a free tier).

name: Cloudflare
help: Create a token at https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens with only the permissions you want agents to have.
